Eversong Woods (also known as Eversong Forest) is a woodland that stands in perpetual spring, comprising much of the blood elven kingdom of Quel'Thalas, which lies in the northern part of Eastern Kingdoms. At the north end lies the capital of Silvermoon City, and beyond it the Isle of Quel'Danas, where the Sunwell can be found. The blood elves have called the resplendent Eversong home for millennia, but the stewardship of this forested region has not been without its perils. Prince Arthas and the Scourge carved a path of destruction during the Scourge invasion of Quel'Thalas, leaving a tainted scar across Eversong Woods and corrupting the southern reaches into the haunted Ghostlands, but recent years have seen the forest restored by the power of the Sunwell.
In World of Warcraft: Midnight, Eversong Woods has been revamped to combine the original Eversong Woods zone with the Ghostlands, and is now connected to the rest of the Eastern Kingdoms.

{{Combat}} [[Sanctum of the Moon]] | affiliation = [[Quel'Thalas (kingdom)|Kingdom of Quel'Thalas]], [[Horde]], [[Silver Covenant]], [[Alliance]], [[Amani tribe]], [[Amani Empire]], [[Twilight's Blade]] | loc = Northern [[Eastern Kingdoms]] }} '''Eversong Woods''' (also known as '''Eversong Forest''')''[[Tides of Darkness]]'', chapter 14, pg. 207 is a woodland that stands in perpetual spring, comprising much of the [[Blood elf|blood elven]] kingdom of [[Quel'Thalas (kingdom)|Quel'Thalas]], which lies in the northern part of [[Eastern Kingdoms]]. At the north end lies the capital of [[Silvermoon City]], and beyond it the [[Isle of Quel'Danas]], where the [[Sunwell]] can be found. The blood elves have called the resplendent Eversong home for millennia, but the stewardship of this forested region has not been without its perils. [[Arthas Menethil|Prince Arthas]] and the [[Scourge]] carved a path of destruction during the [[Scourge invasion of Quel'Thalas]], leaving a [[Dead Scar|tainted scar]] across Eversong Woods and corrupting the southern reaches into the haunted [[Ghostlands]], but recent years have seen the forest restored by the power of the Sunwell. In ''[[World of Warcraft: Midnight]]'', Eversong Woods has been revamped to combine the [[Eversong Woods (Burning Crusade)|original Eversong Woods]] zone with the Ghostlands, and is now connected to the rest of the Eastern Kingdoms.[https://worldofwarcraft.blizzard.com/en-us/midnight World of Warcraft: Midnight website] ==History== ===Early history=== {{novel-section}} [[File:Light and Shadow - Burning of Quel'Thalas.jpg|thumb|Eversong burned by the enslaved [[red dragon]]s, as seen in ''[[Alleria: Light and Shadow]]''.]] Thousands of years ago, these forests were claimed by the [[Highborne]], eventually naming themselves the [[High elf|high elves]], who battled the resident [[Amani tribe|Amani]] populace and took the land for their own. After creating the [[Sunwell]], the Highborne became nourished, which enabled them to create their cities and shape the forests.''[[World of Warcraft: Exploring Azeroth: The Eastern Kingdoms]]'', pg. 92 The elves established the kingdom of [[Quel'Thalas (kingdom)|Quel'Thalas]], and northern Eversong contained the heart of their empire for millennia; the elves' capital of [[Silvermoon City]] was established at the forest's northernmost tip, near the ocean. In time, the elves interwove their architecture to complement Eversong's natural landscape, blending the natural and their arcane-empowered structures together in beautiful ways. They lived in relative harmony with the creatures of the woodlands.[[Unfortunate Measures]] The [[Magisters|magi]] erected numerous [[runestone]]s throughout Eversong, to serve as a dampening field that would limit the potency of all non-elven magic.''[[Blood of the Highborne]]'' They also magically locked Eversong into a state of perpetual springtime;{{Ref WoWCV1|121}} the trees having gold leaves.''[[World of Warcraft: Sylvanas]]'', pg. 72 Shortly after Quel'Thalas was founded, the elves created a legendary bow named [[Thas'dorah, Legacy of the Windrunners|Thas'dorah]], carved from the bark of the mother tree of Eversong. Named [[Thas'alah]], or Light of the Forest, this tree was the oldest in all Quel'Thalas' woodlands, and its roots absorbed the energy of the Sunwell. From its enchanted branches, the entire region seemed to be bathed in the glow of an eternal spring.[[Tales of the Hunt#Thas'dorah, Legacy of the Windrunners|Tales of the Hunt: Thas'dorah, Legacy of the Windrunners]] ===Second War=== {{novel-section}} Although the woods have seen their share of battle between the elves and their relentless neighbors, the [[forest troll]]s, the region retained a harmonic and peaceful feel for much of its history, standing strong for over 7,000 years. Its defenses were tested during the [[Second War]], in which the edges of the forest mysteriously began to burn. During the war, a fully third''[[Tides of Darkness]]'', chapter 15 of the forest was [[Burning of Quel'Thalas|burned down]] by [[red dragon]]s enslaved by the [[Old Horde]], who managed to reach the northern forest but were unable to overcome Silvermoon's defenses, and the violence was soon quelled. In its aftermath, the Amani, who had allied with the fel-crazed orcs, were mercilessly hunted down within Eversong and beyond. ===Third War=== {{novel-section}} [[File:The Dead Scar.jpg|thumb|left|The [[Dead Scar]] left after the [[Scourge invasion of Quel'Thalas|Fall of Quel'Thalas]].]] During the [[Third War]] in 20 [[ADP]], Eversong lay witness to the horrors that the [[death knight]] [[Arthas Menethil]] brought upon the land during his [[Scourge invasion of Quel'Thalas|invasion of Quel'Thalas]], and the forest had since been permanently scarred by the death wrought by the hordes of undead. A huge, plagued tract of land was torn through the center of Eversong, known as the [[Dead Scar]], which stood in stark contrast to the rest of the forest. Countless elves were slaughtered in Eversong, including their ranger-general, [[Sylvanas Windrunner]]. She was succeeded by [[Grand Magister]] [[Belo'vir Salonar]], who took over the defense of Silvermoon after her death, but the capital was also unable to withstand the Scourge's onslaught. After Arthas had reached his goal on [[Quel'Danas]] and abandoned Quel'Thalas to its fate, the remnants of elves in the woods gathered under the banner of [[Lor'themar Theron|Ranger Lord Lor'themar Theron]], who safeguarded the ruined kingdom while searching for any other survivors. After [[Anasterian Sunstrider|High King Anasterian Sunstrider]] and the [[Convocation of Silvermoon]] had been slain during the onslaught, [[Kael'thas Sunstrider|Prince Kael'thas Sunstrider]] became the rightful ruler and rushed back home from [[Dalaran]] to witness the damage to his kingdom with his own eyes. After he destroyed the corrupted Sunwell, he reunited with his people and renamed them [[sin'dorei]], "blood elves" in [[thalassian]], in honor of all those who had perished. Before his departure, the prince placed Lor'themar in charge of Quel'Thalas, then took their remaining forces to battle alongside the [[Alliance resistance]] in [[Lordaeron]], and later under [[Illidan Stormrage]] in [[Outland]]. Most of the blood elves remained behind with their regent, seeking to reclaim their land. Downtrodden and weakened by an [[Magic addiction|addiction to magic]] that had become apparent after the destruction of the elves' Sunwell, the elves made little progress with this until the return of [[Grand Magister Rommath]], who reinvigorated his people with the use of a technique taught to Kael on Outland, the [[Mana Tap|mana draining]]. The elves gathered their strength and began reclaiming and rebuilding; fortunately, most of Eversong was not beyond healing, and the Scourge's defilement that had ruined the [[Ghostlands]] to the south was halted at [[Elrendar]]. Most of the blood elves remained in Eversong to continue rebuilding, while others turned their attention to the Ghostlands, hoping to drive the Scourge out of their beloved kingdom forever. Large portions of Eversong were reclaimed, and [[Silvermoon City]] rose again, but other threats, some old and some new, were looming on the horizon. ===The Burning Crusade=== {{bc-section}} [[File:The Shepherd's Gate.jpg|thumb|[[Silvermoon City]] after being rebuilt.]] By the Year 26 ADP, much of Eversong has been reclaimed, but not without cost. At this time, Eversong was split between [[Eversong Woods (Burning Crusade)|Eversong Woods]] to the north, and the [[Ghostlands]] to the south.[[The Ghostlands (quest)]] The destruction of the [[Sunwell]] adversely affected some of Eversong's wildlife, along with the elves' [[Mana wyrm|own arcane creations]],[[Reclaiming Sunstrider Isle]] driving many erratic and hostile.[[Unfortunate Measures]] Dealing with this, along with understanding every blood elf's innate [[Magic addiction|addiction to magic]], was among the first things blood elf adventurers had to take care. Eversong was also troubled by the [[Wretched]], a group of disheveled, violent mana-addicts who could not balance their dependency on the arcane. Having grown bold with the advent of the elves' recent losses to the Scourge, the [[Amani tribe|Amani]] forest trolls also made incursions into Eversong, diverting the [[Farstriders]]' attention. A south-western portion of Eversong, now known as the [[Scorched Grove]], was burned by the elves in an effort to halt the corruption and the Scourge's advance; while successful, it also turned the local [[treant]]s hostile. With the Sunwell gone, the elves began using their [[arcane sanctum]]s around Eversong to siphon arcane power from ley lines in Quel'Thalas. They also revitalized several of the [[runestone]]s to heighten their defenses, which had fallen into disrepair. Although much of Eversong was restored, the [[Dead Scar]] remained, and the blood elves looked into ways to heal it,[[Unexpected Results]] but investigating magisters deemed it too tainted and beyond saving.[[Research Notes (quest)]] Roughly half of Silvermoon City was reclaimed; however, its western half remained deteriorated, the Dead Scar slicing through it. The [[Blood Hawks]] seem to be the guards of the forest. ===Wrath of the Lich King=== {{Wotlk-section}} During the second [[Scourge Invasion]] in 27 ADP, Eversong was attacked by the [[Scourge]] and a [[necropolis]], until [[Grand Apothecary Putress]] and the [[Horde]] [[adventurer]]s prepared an anti-plague.[[Silvermoon (quest)]] ===Three Sisters=== {{comic-section}} After the [[Argus Campaign]] in 32 ADP, [[Sylvanas Windrunner|Sylvanas]], [[Vereesa Windrunner|Vereesa]], and [[Alleria Windrunner]] reunited in the forest and traveled through the [[Dead Scar]] to the Ghostlands, fighting Scourge minions along the way.''[[Windrunner: Three Sisters]]'' ===Battle for Azeroth=== {{Bfa-section}} During the [[Fourth War]] in 33 ADP, as part of a [[Heritage of the Sin'dorei|ceremony of remembrance]] held each year in the kingdom, a blood elf [[adventurer]] traveled through Eversong to reenact the defense of their lands during the [[Scourge invasion of Quel'Thalas]]. They experienced the evacuation of [[Fairbreeze Village]], as well as [[Ranger-General]] [[Sylvanas Windrunner]]'s final stand against [[Arthas Menethil]] as the [[high elf]] forces attempted to bar the [[Scourge]]'s rampage.[[The Day Hope Died]] The ceremony then continued on the [[Isle of Quel'Danas]]. ===Midnight=== {{Mn-section}} By the time of the [[War of Light and Shadow]], most of Eversong Woods had finally recovered, and the [[Ghostlands]] had been restored to their former beauty.[https://news.blizzard.com/en-us/article/24223893/explore-the-zones-of-midnight Explore the Zones of Midnight] The restored [[Sunwell]]'s influence imbued the flora of Eversong with the Light, giving rise to what the blood elves called the [[Lightbloom]].[[Fair Breeze, Light Bloom]] Following the emergence of the [[Voidstorm]], the Sunwell's flare-up sent the Lightbloom into a frenzy, causing it to spread rapidly across Eversong and driving the native wildlife into sin'dorei settlements.[[Displaced Denizens]] The [[Farstriders]] launched an operation to investigate the source of the infestation.[[Following the Root]] The Lightbloom's wood also attracted the attention of [[Zul'jan]] of the [[Amani tribe]], who sought to harvest the lightwood to forge weapons capable of defeating the [[Twilight's Blade]]. He personally led the logging operation,[[A Foe Unseen]] but his actions sent the Lightbloom into a frenzy, which caused it to destroy [[Suncrown]]. And so his forces were attacked by the blood elves and the [[Vanguard of the Light]] to avenge the fallen.[[Past Redemption]] ==Geography== ===Maps and subregions=== [[File:VZ-Eversong.jpg|thumb|Zone map]] {| class="darktable hlist" | *[[Amani Pass]] *[[Azurebreeze Coast]] *[[Brightwing Estate]] *[[Daggerspine Landing]] *[[Daggerspine Point]] *[[Dawnstar Spire]] *[[East Sanctum]] *[[Elrendar River]] *[[Fairbreeze Village]] *[[Farstrider Enclave]] *[[Farstrider Hold]] *[[Goldenbough Pass]] *[[Goldenmist Village]] *[[Hollow Grove]] *[[Lake Elrendar]] *[[Lightbloom Ath'Ran]] *[[Lightbloom Lash'Ra]] *[[North Sanctum]] *[[Path of Dawn]] *[[Ruins of Deatholme]] *[[Runestone Falithas]] *[[Runestone Shan'dor]] *[[Saltheril's Haven]] *[[Sanctum of the Moon]] *[[Sanctum of the Sun]] *[[Scintilas Falls]] *[[Scintilas Outpost]] *[[Silverglade Refuge]] *[[Solaarian Sunbath]] *[[Stillwhisper Pond]] *[[Suncrown]] *[[Suncrown Tree]] *[[Sunfeather Point]] *[[Sunsail Anchorage]] *[[Sunset Strand]] *[[Sunstrider Isle]] *[[Thalassian Pass]] *[[Thalassian Range]] *[[Great Sea|The Great Sea]] *[[Thuron's Livery]] *[[Tor'Watha]] *[[Tranquil Repose]] *[[Tranquillien]] *[[Watha'nan Crypts]] *[[West Sanctum]] *[[Windrunner Spire]] *[[Windrunner Village]] *[[Zeb'Nowa]] *[[Zeb'tela Ruins]] |} File:VZ-Silvermoon.jpg|Silvermoon City ===Adjacent regions=== {| class="darktable zebra" |- ! Razed by dragonfire in the [[Second War]] and ravaged by undead in the [[Third War]], the land is a dead, ghostly realm. No living creatures, not even animals, remain in this haunted region. The spirits of slaughtered elves roam the landscape like mist given form and voice.''[[Lands of Conflict]]'', pg. 112 When the [[forest troll]]s of [[Zul'Aman]] raised again, the [[Farstriders]] stopped them in Eversong Forest in southern [[Quel'Thalas]].''[[Dark Factions]]'', pg. 153 ==Notes and trivia== *[[Sylvanas Windrunner]] was named after the woods of her homeland, and she considered the forest to be beautiful.''[[World of Warcraft: Sylvanas]]'', pg. 52 *The [[Tranquillien Archer's Bow]] was carved from the pristine white branches of Eversong Woods. ==Gallery== File:Eversong Woods concept art 1.jpg|Concept art by [[Alexander Winkler]].
